column1: # Kolima home interiors: villagers trapped as trees, Mind Read, logging, family arguments, post-cure visitors and examine text.

column3: A book about the holy\ntrees. It explains how Tret\nand Laurel guard Kolima{page_break}Forest.{end_wait}
A guide to the trees and\nflowers of Angara, with\ndrawings in the margins.{end_wait}
A book about logging. It\nwarns that a good\nlumberjack must know which{page_break}trees to leave standing.{end_wait}
Fuchin Temple is across the\nriver. They say the master\nthere understands how the{page_break}forest has changed.{end_wait}
We were proud of that\nbridge. Now I keep thinking\nabout how many trees we cut{page_break}to build it.{end_wait}
I spent days standing in\nthe sun, unable to move. I\nnever noticed how warm it{page_break}was before.{end_wait}

McCoy stopped work on his
palace. That means the
hired lumberjacks will{page_break}leave. I can't say I blame
them.{end_wait}

They say travelers from the
Goma Range saved us. Every
person who tells it makes{page_break}the warriors a little
bigger.{end_wait}
I heard the heroes were\ngiants with beards down to\ntheir chests. What? You've{page_break}met them?{end_wait}
You saved the village? Then\nI ought to tell you my\nsecret. Maybe later. My{page_break}wife might hear.{end_wait}
My husband keeps whispering\nabout something he found. I\nwish he'd just tell me.{end_wait}
Daddy told me his secret.\nHe made me promise not to\ntell Mother.{end_wait}
I won't pick up an axe\nagain. Not after what we\ndid to Tret.{end_wait}
Dad, if you stop cutting\nwood, how will we pay for\nfood?{end_wait}
You can't just quit work,\nDad. We still need to eat.{end_wait}
The palace work is over.\nMaybe Kolima will be quiet\nagain. I hope the{page_break}shopkeepers can manage.{end_wait}

I came to Kolima for
logging work. Now I'm going
back to my family in Imil.{page_break}I've had enough of this
place.{end_wait}
I was here buying lumber\nwhen the curse struck. The\nmoment the roads are clear,{page_break}I'm heading for Xian.{end_wait}
I couldn't tell you who\nsaved us. But I know they\ndidn't have beards as big{page_break}as people say.{end_wait}
A hero has to be tall. And\nhave a beard. Everyone\nknows that. Don't they?{end_wait}
It's buried deep in the\nforest. If my wife finds\nout, I'll never hear the{page_break}end of it.{end_wait}
He found something\nvaluable. I know he did.\nNow he pretends he doesn't{page_break}remember.{end_wait}
He only says it's somewhere\noutside town. That could\nmean anywhere.{end_wait}
My axe was part of this. I\ncan't pretend otherwise.\nBut I still have a family{page_break}to feed.{end_wait}
He says he'll never cut\nanother tree. Wait until we\nhave nothing for supper.{end_wait}
How can I grow if I don't\neat? Dad can't feed us by\nmaking promises.{end_wait}
The master at Fuchin Temple\nis said to be a strange\nman. I wonder if he knows{page_break}what happened here.{end_wait}
We cut so many trees to\nbuild that bridge. I never\nthought a tree might{page_break}remember.{end_wait}
I was afraid when I became\na tree. Still, I remember\nsunlight on my leaves. That{page_break}part was almost pleasant.{end_wait}

Everyone made good money
when the palace work
started. Then Tret cursed{page_break}us. What was any of it
worth?{end_wait}
Quiet means poor for a town\nlike this. I wanted more\nwork, not for anyone to get{page_break}hurt.{end_wait}
I'm a lumberjack. It's what\nI know. I just need to find\na way to work without{page_break}hurting the forest.{end_wait}
Those stones from the sky\nmust be worth something. I\nwonder if anyone kept one.{end_wait}

I dreamed a huge warrior
with a bushy beard would
save us. I keep hoping{page_break}he'll walk through the
door.{end_wait}
My savings are hidden under\nthe floorboards. If I'm\nstuck like this, who gets{page_break}them?{end_wait}
Father says he has a\nsecret. It's almost worse\nthan being stuck in this{page_break}house.{end_wait}
At least Dad never tried\ncutting down Tret himself.\nI wish that made me feel{page_break}safer.{end_wait}
Father was right about\nTret. I just didn't know\nthe holy tree could do{page_break}something like this.{end_wait}
I'm turning into a tree in\nmy own room. I can't even\nstretch my branches!{end_wait}
Someone must have hurt\nTret. Why would anyone try\ncutting down our holy tree?{end_wait}
How am I supposed to run an\ninn when I can't even lift\na finger?{end_wait}
We knew cutting Tret was\nwrong. I went with the\nothers anyway. Now I may{page_break}never see Imil again.{end_wait}
If I'd checked out\nyesterday, I'd be halfway\nto Xian by now. All because{page_break}I liked that bed.{end_wait}
